name: Pack Ice Field
description: A vast Arctic sea-ice field, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — an endless plain of broken white and pale-blue pack ice, jagged pressure ridges heaving up in angular slabs, and dark cracks and leads of black open water cutting across the surface, realistic ice and snow texture. A flat white horizon under an open sky. No people, no structures. Lighting-neutral (used across day, storm, and dusk scenes).

name: Greenland Ice Cap
description: The vast interior ice cap of Greenland, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a smooth, rolling plateau of unbroken white snow stretching to a flat horizon, gentle wind-carved ridges and low snow drifts, distant pale-blue mountains at the far edges, realistic snow texture. Wider and smoother than broken sea ice, with no open water. No people, no structures. Lighting-neutral.

name: Night Ice Camp
description: A small Arctic camp on the sea ice seen at NIGHT under deep moonlight, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a low dome tent or a small snow-block shelter, a wooden sledge parked beside it, faint tracks in the snow, realistic canvas and wood texture. Deep desaturated navy-blue and indigo night tones throughout, a pale moon and scattered stars overhead, cold blue shadows on the snow — NOT daylight, NOT sunny, NOT a bright blue sky. No people in the base image.

name: Annoatok Base
description: A small remote Arctic expedition base on the rocky Greenland coast, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — one or two low wooden and stone huts with turf roofs, wooden crates and barrels stacked outside, drying racks, a snowy rocky shoreline meeting frozen sea in the background, realistic wood, stone, and turf texture. Lighting-neutral (used in different seasons). No people in the base image.

name: Ship Deck
description: The wooden deck of a turn-of-the-century polar expedition ship, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — weathered wooden planking, thick rope rigging, a tall mast, a coiled anchor chain, wooden crates and barrels lashed down, a metal railing, and frozen sea visible beyond the rail, realistic weathered wood, rope, and metal texture. Lighting-neutral. No people in the base image.

name: New York Harbor
description: An early-1900s New York harbor, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a busy wooden dock with tall-masted sail-and-steam ships, wooden pilings, stacked cargo crates and barrels, coiled ropes, and a skyline of low brick warehouses and early skyscrapers with smokestacks in the background, realistic weathered wood, brick, and metal texture. Lighting-neutral (day-dominant). No people in the base image.

name: The Newsroom
description: A busy early-1900s newspaper office, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — rows of wooden desks piled with papers, black cast-iron typewriters, a large printing press with rollers and gears against the back wall, stacks of freshly printed broadsheets, hanging electric bulb lamps, and tall windows, realistic wood, iron, and paper texture. Lighting-neutral. No people in the base image.

name: The Banquet Hall
description: An opulent 1900s New York banquet hall, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a long formal dining table draped in white cloth set with silver and candlesticks, ornate gilded columns and moulding, large crystal chandeliers glowing warmly, deep red carpet and drapery, realistic fabric, gilt, and crystal texture, a warm amber golden atmosphere. No people in the base image.

name: The Press Room
description: A grand hotel press-conference room in the Waldorf Astoria style, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — an elegant paneled room with a raised podium and a small table at the front, rows of wooden chairs facing it, tall draped windows, warm electric wall sconces, realistic wood paneling and fabric texture, and a formal refined atmosphere. Distinct from a dining hall — no long banquet table. No people in the base image.

name: The Ceremony Stage
description: A formal early-1900s awards ceremony stage and auditorium, photographed in a cinematic, photorealistic documentary style — a raised wooden stage with a draped lectern and large American-flag bunting behind it, a decorative arch, rows of theater seating fading into the background, realistic wood and fabric texture, warm stage lighting from above. Distinct from both a dining hall and a press room. No people in the base image.
